_batch: For a saline-filled chip: everything short, one of each kind of presentation, so the recording can be checked with `report`. Run `select --centers` (no scan, no baseline) to fill regions and rec_electrodes. Run once as is, then again with dt_cs_us 20 to exercise the unit-switching path, and once with t_stim 600, encode_pattern [PAIR], encode_cycles 1 to see that a full-length sequence loads.
_phase_lead_min: Quiet at the start of each encode recording when the session is split; short here so the dry run's four files stay short.
description: dry run on saline: does every presentation fire where and when it should
_rec_electrodes: Filled in by `select`. Every electrode to record; the regions' patches plus a spread over the rest.
_regions: Centres in um, x along the long axis (0-3832), y along the short (0-2082). Filled in by `select`; then keep them fixed for the culture.
_stim_electrodes: Filled in by `select` (the planned 2x2 per region) and rewritten by `run` with the electrodes it actually connected, when a stimulation unit clash made it swap one for a routed neighbour. Honoured only while stim_electrodes_site equals stim_site; delete both to rebuild the sites from the centres.
_routing_cfg: Written by `run`: the routing it solved, saved as a MaxLab .cfg in the work directory. Later runs load it instead of routing again, so the stimulation units, and so the driven electrodes, are the same every time. Delete it (or re-run `select`) to route afresh.
_amplitudes_mv: Per role, mV PER PHASE; peak to peak is twice this. Ronchi et al. 2019 characterised 40-240 mV peak to peak (20-120 per phase) on these arrays; the ladder runs 10-100 per phase and max_amplitude_mv refuses anything above 120 per phase unless raised deliberately.
_amplitude_thresholds_mv: Per region, the lowest amplitude calibration found usable: the lowest at which the whole site evoked a countable response over the region's 150 um disc. Written by `report --apply` alongside amplitudes_mv. `preview` prints the chosen amplitude as a multiple of it, which is the headroom. It is an amplitude measured on a site against a population count, not the field at which a neuron fires, so nothing here converts it into a radius.
_amplitudes_source: Where amplitudes_mv came from: the calibration recording's name once `report --apply` has written it. 'default' means nobody calibrated, and a conditioning run refuses to start. 'saline' is the dry run's stand-in.
_field_model: Path to the JSON written by `fieldmap report --save-model`: how the potential falls off through the medium, measured on a saline chip (an exponent and uV per mV at one electrode pitch). Optional. With it, `preview` shades the array with the potential the pulses put on it and prints what each site puts at the other two. A saline map says nothing about what field fires a neuron; run the same map on a culture to see how tissue changes the falloff.
_stim_site: What stimulates a region. hex (the default): seven driven electrodes, one at the centre and six around it gap+1 electrodes away in rows of 2-3-2, 210 um across at gap 5; seven per site, 21 of the chip's 32 stimulation units. Seven spread over a disc rather than four at a square's corners, because an electrode that is not over a neuron or an axon stimulates nothing. grid: a size x size block, gap empty electrodes between them. focal: {shape, inner, inner_gap, return_radius, return_points} adds return electrodes carrying the inverted pulse to confine the field (Ronchi et al. 2019) at the cost of more units. The chip hands units out per area of the array (about seven per area, measured on a MaxOne), so a dense site may not connect; run swaps clashing electrodes for routed neighbours and says so, and a wider gap spreads the site over more of the chip. Widen a site with gap, never with more electrodes.
_stim_phase_us: Biphasic, charge balanced. 100 us per phase is enough and keeps the artifact short; anodic-first was the more effective order in voltage mode (Ronchi et al. 2019).
_pulse_hz: A presentation is t_stim (training) or t_probe (probe) seconds of pulse events at pulse_hz. pulses_per_burst 1 is a single pulse per event; 11 at burst_hz 20 is a Jimbo-style tetanus.
_mode: conditioning, or calibration: single pulses at every calibration amplitude and polarity, per region.
_pre_min: Minutes. probe_iti, encode_iti, encode_cycle_rest, calibration_iti, t_stim, t_probe are seconds; dt_cs_us and the windows are ms.
_probe_roles: Each probe is t_probe seconds at pulse_hz (20 pulses); probe_reps of each role per block gives 60 probe pulses per role to estimate a response probability from. Retrieval probes all three roles so a US-alone change in excitability is not read as learning. Every probe is also a little extinction, so keep probe pulses small next to the paired ones.
_encode_pattern: encode_cycles cycles of encode_pattern (encode_iti apart) then encode_cycle_rest seconds of nothing. Sized for a four-hour first session that should teach the culture something if anything will: three cycles of 10 min pairing, 10 min pairing, 10 min NS at 0.33 Hz, 5 min rest; 60 min and 1200 paired pulses. Cut encode_cycles or a retrieval block for a shorter run, not t_stim. encode_iti must cover t_stim; probe_iti must cover t_probe plus the response windows.
_calibration_amplitudes_mv: mV per phase (peak to peak is twice). Seven rungs from 10 to 100: starts low because thresholds on these arrays can sit near the bottom of Ronchi's 40-240 mV peak-to-peak range, and stops at 100 because above that the response saturates and pulses start bursts. max_amplitude_mv 120 (240 pp, the top of Ronchi's range) is the hard stop.
_calibration_polarities: Both. The report picks, per region, the polarity that reaches threshold with less voltage (anodic-first on a tie) and writes it to pulse_polarity with --apply. Anodic-first is the literature's answer, but which DAC direction is 'anodic' at the electrode on this rig is unconfirmed, so the sweep decides rather than the label.
_calibration_reps: Repeats of the whole (region x amplitude x polarity) set; each repeat is shuffled and the regions interleaved. 6 repeats x 7 amplitudes x 2 polarities = 84 single pulses per region, 252 in all, 12.6 min at calibration_iti 3 s -- about a twelfth of the conditioning session's pulses.
_raw_traces: spikes are always kept, for every routed channel. raw_traces adds raw voltage: none (spikes only, ~1 MB a minute; the readout needs nothing more), regions (the three regions' recording and stimulation electrodes, enough to see the stimulation artifact), all (every channel: ~4 kB per channel-second on a MaxTwo, twice on a MaxOne, tens of GB for a four-hour run). The dry run keeps region traces because its artifact check is the point of it.
_pulse_window_ms: Counted after every pulse of a presentation and summed: the readout. response_windows_ms is optional; without it the windows are base/during/after sized by t_probe.
